title: Build for November interviews
summary: One defensible AI flagship first. Add a compact ML lifecycle project when capacity allows. Keep coding, fundamentals, and interview practice active throughout.
capacity_note: 10 hours/week is the existing provisional setting; availability is not yet confirmed. Milestones are not single-day tasks. Selective earlier applications remain welcome.

budgets.outcome: Small flagship; second project can continue in November.
Flagship, compact ML project, repeated mocks.
Both projects plus targeted depth and interview loops.

weeks.outcome: Baseline assessment; audit existing code; choose one workflow and dataset.
Working document-to-answer or extraction path with source references.
Frozen evaluation set, baseline comparison, error analysis and measured improvement.
Durable workflow state, bounded tools, failure recovery and authorization tests.
Deploy flagship and rehearse rollback; start ML project only if ready and capacity allows.
Close the largest weakness; complete the compact ML project at higher capacity.
Feature freeze, independent retests, demo and role-specific readiness review.
Main application/interview campaign; repair weaknesses revealed by real feedback.

projects.title: 1. Evidence Workbench
projects.estimate: 30–45 focused build hours for a narrow version if usable code exists; reassess after the baseline audit.
projects.goal: Turn financial or industrial documents into structured, source-backed answers and reviewed draft reports.
projects.stack: Python API, Postgres, a worker, a minimal web interface, one model provider and one deployment environment.

milestones.text: Confirm one user workflow, public/licensed data, schema, baseline and reproducible local run.
Ingest and deduplicate documents; extract/index; return source-backed answers with a human review step.
Create 30–50 reviewed evaluation tasks with separate held-out documents; compare baseline and improved workflow.
Demonstrate duplicate, timeout, worker interruption, malformed output and authorization failure handling.
Deploy, measure latency and cost per successful task, capture redacted traces and demonstrate rollback.
Record a five-minute demo, three architecture decisions and one failure analysis; independently rebuild a critical function.

projects.defer: Go gateway, Kafka, Spark, Kubernetes and multiple agents until a measured constraint or specific interview justifies them.

projects.title: 2. Decision Model
projects.estimate: 20–30 focused build hours after data access is confirmed. At 10 hours/week, continue into November.
projects.goal: Demonstrate the complete lifecycle of one useful tabular prediction problem, from validation to serving and rollback.
projects.stack: Python, a simple baseline and one stronger model, reproducible feature code, a versioned model artifact, API or batch scoring.

milestones.text: Define decision, label and leakage risks; select a defensible temporal, grouped or random split based on the data.
Compare a simple baseline and one stronger model on held-out data; analyze errors and uncertainty.
Use consistent training/serving features; validate inputs, version artifacts and measure performance.
Demonstrate monitoring and rollback; explain when evidence warrants retraining.
Reproduce results from a clean run and defend model selection, limitations and deployment tradeoffs.

projects.defer: Distributed training and multiple GPU runtimes; choose at most one targeted serving or fine-tuning lab after core readiness.

first_session: Two hours: Python 25m, SQL 20m, validation/leakage explanation 20m, architecture sketch 15m, existing-code audit 30m, scope choice 10m.
optional: At most one 6–10 hour extension before the main campaign: GPU serving, fine-tuning, a tiny transformer, autonomous coding or voice. Choose it for a concrete role or observed gap.
readiness: Independently solve and test role-appropriate tasks, explain model validation, defend architecture under changed constraints, and tell six factual experience stories. These are practice checks, not guarantees of interview outcomes.
